children: , the heavy-equipment maker, put a remotely operated dozer to work at an Arizona landfill as its shares rose about 0.8% to $811.58 at 11.50 am ET time on Friday. The machine lets an operator move waste from a control station away from the heat, dust and unstable ground.

The landfill is one test of Caterpillar's technology. WM says it is working with Caterpillar to test an autonomous compactor after piloting the remote-controlled dozer. At Luck Stone's Bull Run quarry, autonomous trucks have hauled more than 3.5 million tons since November 2024. The companies are now expanding the system to two more Virginia sites.

That expansion is a stronger commercial signal than a single pilot, but Caterpillar has not put a dollar figure on these deployments. Investors still need evidence that wider use brings meaningful service revenue or productivity gains. At $811.58, the shares stand 75.98% above the $461.18 GF Value estimatea steep price for progress that has yet to be quantified.

title: Caterpillar Stock Gains as Remote Autonomy Leaves the Cab
